title: Spiritual Growth
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Spiritual growth is the believer’s increasing maturity in faith, love, holiness, wisdom, obedience, and likeness to Christ. It is God’s ongoing work in His people as they respond to His Word, Spirit, grace, and discipline.
summary: Spiritual growth is the believer’s increasing maturity in faith, love, holiness, wisdom, obedience, and likeness to Christ. It is God’s ongoing work in His people as they respond to His Word, Spirit, grace, and discipline.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is both the source and goal of spiritual growth. Believers grow up into Him, become more like Him, and bear fruit through life in union with Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God intends His children to grow. New life in Christ is not meant to remain immature, shallow, or fruitless. Believers are called to increase in knowledge, holiness, love, discernment, and faithfulness.

Spiritual growth happens through ordinary means of grace: Scripture, prayer, obedience, fellowship, suffering, service, correction, and the work of the Holy Spirit. Growth is often gradual, but God is faithful to continue His work.

Maturity is not measured only by information or activity. A growing believer becomes more like Christ in character, humility, endurance, love, wisdom, and obedience.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers become discouraged because growth feels slow. Others mistake busyness or knowledge for maturity. Scripture gives a better vision: God grows His people over time by grace.

This doctrine encourages perseverance. The Christian life is not instant perfection, but faithful growth under the hand of God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue growth with patience and diligence. Stay in Scripture, pray honestly, obey what God shows you, receive correction, and remain connected to the body of Christ. Do not despise small steps of faithfulness; trust God to continue the work He began.
